entities.summary:
Rodrigo de Bastidas was a Spanish conquistador and explorer who mapped the northern coast of South America, discovering Panama and founding the city of Santa Marta. Born in unknown, he spent his life in the service of the Spanish Crown, tasked with expanding Spanish influence in the New World. His expeditions took him to the Pacific coast of South America, where he encountered indigenous peoples and established trade routes. De Bastidas's legacy as a conquistador has been the subject of ongoing debate among historians.

De Bastidas was a key figure in the Spanish colonization of South America, playing a crucial role in the establishment of the Viceroyalty of New Granada. His expeditions and discoveries helped to lay the foundations for Spanish dominance in the region. However, his legacy is also marked by controversy, as he was instrumental in the displacement and marginalization of indigenous populations.

De Bastidas's impact on the region can still be seen today, as the city of Santa Marta remains a significant cultural and economic hub in Colombia. His discovery of Panama also had far-reaching consequences, as it opened up new trade routes and helped to establish Spain as a major power in the Americas.

In the end, De Bastidas's life and legacy serve as a reminder of the complex and often fraught history of Spanish colonization in South America.
